reply.text:
Done.

The bug was auto-retry: `resource()` had `retry: { attempts: 3, backoff: Backoff.Exponential }`, so a single refused request silently retried itself back to success (or masked the failure) instead of surfacing the error — which broke all three behaviours you flagged.

Fixes in `modules/customers/`:
- **`customers.effects.ts`** — dropped the `retry` option from `loadCustomers()`. One failed request now fails once, immediately; the only second attempt is a person clicking Retry (`list.invalidate()`), which the resource always turns into exactly one new request.
- **`customers.state.ts`** — added a `loading` transition, since a retry re-enters `resource`'s `'loading'` status and the state needs to reflect that (not sit on the stale `error`).
- **`customers.effects.ts`** — `commitList` now also handles `list.is('loading')` → `state.loading()`, so the view's loader shows again during a retry, keeping loading/error/table strictly exclusive.
- Updated the unit tests (`customers.state.test.ts`, `customers.effects.test.ts`) to match: a refusal fails after exactly one request, and retry produces exactly one more.

Verified against the live app at `127.0.0.1:56077` with Playwright, reproducing each scenario from the behaviour tests you named (one-time 500, 800ms latency, MutationObserver overlap tracking): all four passed — refused load shows only the error with 1 request, retry issues exactly 1 more request and the list arrives, and loading/error/table are never visible together through the whole failure→retry→success cycle. `sheratan check`, `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and the unit suite are all clean.
